summary.one_liner: Pulp is an open source audio sample manager, built with Tauri, that scans folders, indexes audio files, and helps organize and search them.
summary.what_it_does: Pulp scans a folder you choose, retrieves the audio files in it, and lets you organize and search them. It is described as an alternative to ADSR Sample Manager and also works as an audio file explorer. The README lists cross-platform support for Windows, macOS (Intel and Silicon), and Linux, plus a modern interface. Automatic detection of BPM and key is listed as a planned feature, not a current one. The back end uses Tauri, Prisma, and SQLite, and the front end uses Solid-JS. The README also says a version 2 with more improvements is in development and is not open source yet.
use_cases: managing a sample library for music production
browsing and organizing audio files in folders
searching a collection of audio samples
replacing ADSR Sample Manager with an open source tool
how_to_run: Rename src-tauri/.env.dist to src-tauri/.env and set DATABASE_URL (macOS path per README)
npm run cargo -- prisma migrate dev --name init
npm run cargo -- prisma generate && npm run prisma-js -- generate
notable: Open source alternative to ADSR Sample Manager
Cross-platform desktop app for Windows, macOS, and Linux
Doubles as an audio file explorer, not only a sample manager
Includes VS Code debugging configuration in the .vscode folder
Helper npm script wraps cargo and prisma commands
caveats: Automatic BPM and key detection is marked as coming soon
Setup is multi-step: Rust/cargo, npm, Prisma migrations, and a manual DATABASE_URL edit
A v2 is in development and is not open source yet
The README describes the database path setup for macOS in detail; other OSes need manual path adjustment
